{{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|ar|أتسوتا-كو|ca|Atsuta-ku|ceb|Atsuta-ku|es|Atsuta-ku (Nagoya)|fa|آتسوتا-کو، ناگویا|fr|Atsuta-ku|id|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|it|Atsuta-ku|ja|熱田区|ko|아쓰타구|pl|Atsuta (Nagoja)|th|เขตอัตสึตะ|tl|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|tr|Atsuta|uk|Район Ацута|ur|اتسوتا وارڈ، ناگویا|vi|Atsuta, Nagoya|zh|热田区|qid=Q1355625|lt=Atsuta Ward}} {{ill|Takakura-chō|ja|高蔵町 (名古屋市)|qid=Q56449178|lt=Takakura-cho}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}) and a Keigai-Sessha of {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|abstract|Q482065|ar|أتسوتا جينغو|az|Atsuta məbədi|cs|Svatyně Acuta|de|Atsuta-jingū|eu|Atsuta santutegia|fa|معبد آتسوتا|fr|Atsuta-jingū|hu|Acutai nagyszentély|id|Kuil Atsuta|it|Santuario di Atsuta|ja|熱田神宮|ko|아쓰타 신궁|la|Atsuta Templum|or|ଆତ୍ସୁତା ଶାଳ|pl|Atsuta-jingū|pt|Santuário de Atsuta|simple|Atsuta Shrine|th|ศาลเจ้าอัตสึตะ|tr|Atsuta Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ацута|zh|熱田神宮|qid=Q482065|lt=Atsuta Shrine}}.

Like Atsuta Shrine, it enshrines the ancestral deity of Owari. Serving as the guardian and tutelary deity of the Takakura area, it is deeply revered locally and affectionately called “Takakura-sama.”

== Worshipped deities (Saijin) ==
{{see also|{{ill|Saijin|abstract|Q11591100|fr|Saijin|ja|祭神|zh|祭神|qid=Q11591100}}}}
The enshrined deity is the following one figure<ref name="HistoryDocument">Shrine History Document.</ref>:
* '''{{ill|Takakuraji|fr|Takakuraji|it|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|zh|高倉下|qid=Q11668757|lt=Takakura-shita-no-mikoto}}''' (Takakura-shita-no-mikoto)

== History ==
=== Founding ===
The founding is unknown. According to tradition, it may date to the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ar|الإمبراطور تيمو|arz|الامبراطور تيمو|azb|تمو|ca|Tenmu|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر تێنمو|cs|Temmu|de|Temmu|eo|Temmu|es|Tenmu Tennō|fa|امپراتور تنمو|fr|Tenmu|hak|Tenmu Thiên-fòng|he|טמו, קיסר יפן|hu|Tenmu japán császár|id|Kaisar Tenmu|it|Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|ka|ტენმუ|ko|덴무 천황|la|Tenmu (imperator)|nl|Tenmu|pl|Tenmu|pt|Tenmu|ru|Император Тэмму|sh|Car Temmu|simple|Emperor Tenmu|sl|Cesar Tenmu|su|Kaisar Temmu|sv|Tenmu|th|จักรพรรดิเท็มมุ|tl|Emperador Temmu|tr|Temmu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Темму|vi|Thiên hoàng Tenmu|yo|Emperor Temmu|zh|天武天皇|zh_min_nan|Tenmu Thian-hông|zh_yue|天武天皇|qid=Q335181}} (673–686)<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>, or it is said to have been established around the same time as the main shrine of Atsuta Shrine{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}.

Regarding the Keigai-Sessha of Atsuta Shrine—including Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine—there is a theory correlating its origins with the distribution of various Owari powers during the Kofun period<ref name="NagoyaHistoryVolume1 486-488"/>. In this context, it is speculated that the dominant forces on the Atsuta plateau (such as {{ill|Danpusan Kofun|fr|Kofun de Danpusan|ja|断夫山古墳|qid=Q5221001|lt=Danpusan Kofun}}, {{ill|Shiratori Kofun (Nagoya)|ja|白鳥古墳 (名古屋市)|qid=Q11580543|lt=Hakuchou Kofun}}, and {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|abstract|Q482065|ar|أتسوتا جينغو|az|Atsuta məbədi|cs|Svatyně Acuta|de|Atsuta-jingū|eu|Atsuta santutegia|fa|معبد آتسوتا|fr|Atsuta-jingū|hu|Acutai nagyszentély|id|Kuil Atsuta|it|Santuario di Atsuta|ja|熱田神宮|ko|아쓰타 신궁|la|Atsuta Templum|or|ଆତ୍ସୁତା ଶାଳ|pl|Atsuta-jingū|pt|Santuário de Atsuta|simple|Atsuta Shrine|th|ศาลเจ้าอัตสึตะ|tr|Atsuta Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ацута|zh|熱田神宮|qid=Q482065|lt=Atsuta Shrine}}) absorbed other powers, resulting in the incorporation of various shrines into Atsuta Shrine’s divine genealogy<ref name="NagoyaHistoryVolume1 486-488">Shinshu Nagoya City History, Volume 1, Nagoya City, 1997, pp. 486–488.</ref>.

=== General History ===
According to the national histories ({{ill|Rikkokushi|cs|Rikkokuši|de|Rikkokushi|es|Rikkokushi|eu|Rikkokushi|fa|شش تاریخ ملی|fr|Rikkokushi|it|Rikkokushi|ja|六国史|ko|육국사|pt|Rikkokushi|ru|Риккокуси|simple|Rikkokushi|zh|六國史|qid=Q1151168|lt=National Histories}}), the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|cs|Šoku Nihonkóki|de|Shoku Nihon Kōki|es|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ff|Shoku Nihon Kōki|fr|Shoku nihon kōki|ja|続日本後紀|ko|속일본후기|pt|Shoku Nihon Kōki|zh|續日本後紀|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}} in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|de|Jōwa|es|Jōwa (período Heian)|fa|جووا (دوره هی‌آن)|fr|Ère Jōwa (Heian)|ia|Jowa|id|Jōwa|ja|承和 (日本)|ko|조와 (834년)|ru|Дзёва (Хэйан)|simple|Jōwa (Heian period)|sr|Џова (Хејан период)|tr|Jōwa (Heian)|uk|Дзьова (ненґо)|zh|承和 (日本)|zh_yue|承和|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} (836) contains a passage listing three deities of Atsuta Shrine—the Hiwari-mikogami, Mago-waka-mikogami, and the deity of Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Atsuta Ōkami Mikogami) – among the renowned deities{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

In the {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5th year (927) version of the ''Engishiki'' ({{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}), in Owari Province’s {{ill|Aichi District|ceb|Aichi-gun|de|Aichi-gun|es|Distrito de Aichi (Aichi)|fa|شهرستان آیچی، آیچی|fr|District d'Aichi|hu|Aicsi körzet|id|Distrik Aichi, Aichi|it|Distretto di Aichi|ja|愛知郡 (愛知県)|ko|아이치군|pl|Powiat Aichi|ru|Айти (уезд)|tl|Distrito ng Aichi, Aichi|uk|Повіт Айті|vi|Aichi (huyện)|zh|愛知郡 (愛知縣)|qid=Q552687|lt=Aichi District}}, it is recorded as “Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine Myoujindai” and is listed alongside the {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}. Moreover, in the {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|尾張国内神名帳|sv|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|zh|尾張國內神名帳|qid=Q11041830}}, it is recorded either as “Takakura Myōjin” or “Takakura Myōjin”{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}.

During the construction in the {{ill|Genki (era)|ckb|گێنکی (سەردەم)|fa|گنکی|fr|Ère Genki|ja|元亀|ko|겐키|ru|Гэнки (эра)|simple|Genki|sr|Генки|sv|Genki|tr|Genki|zh|元龜|qid=Q1145064|lt=Genki era}} 2nd year (1571), there was a donation from {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|af|Oda Nobunaga|ar|أودا نوبوناغا|arz|اودا نوبوناجا|ast|Oda Nobunaga|az|Oda Nobunaqa|ban|Oda Nobunaga|bcl|Oda Nobunaga|be|Ода Набунага|bg|Ода Нобунага|bs|Oda Nobunaga|ca|Oda Nobunaga|cdo|Cék-dièng Séng-diòng|ckb|ئۆدا نۆبوناگا|cs|Nobunaga Oda|da|Oda Nobunaga|de|Oda Nobunaga|el|Όντα Νομπουνάγκα|eo|Oda Nobunaga|es|Oda Nobunaga|et|Oda Nobunaga|eu|Oda Nobunaga|fa|اودا نوبوناگا|fi|Oda Nobunaga|fr|Oda Nobunaga|gl|Oda Nobunaga|glk|اؤدا نؤبۊناگا|hak|Oda Nobunaga|he|אודה נובונאגה|hr|Oda Nobunaga|hu|Oda Nobunaga|id|Oda Nobunaga|is|Oda Nobunaga|it|Oda Nobunaga|ja|織田信長|ka|ოდა ნობუნაგა|kk|Ода Нобунага|ko|오다 노부나가|kw|Oda Nobunaga|la|Nobunanga|lt|Oda Nobunaga|lv|Oda Nobunaga|mg|Oda Nobunaga|mn|Ода Нобүнага|ms|Oda Nobunaga|nl|Oda Nobunaga|no|Oda Nobunaga|oc|Oda Nobunaga|pam|Nobunaga Oda|pl|Nobunaga Oda|pt|Oda Nobunaga|ro|Nobunaga Oda|ru|Ода Нобунага|sc|Oda Nobunaga|sh|Nobunaga Oda|simple|Oda Nobunaga|sk|Nobunaga Oda|sq|Oda Nobunaga|sr|Ода Нобунага|su|Oda Nobunaga|sv|Oda Nobunaga|tg|Ода Набунага|th|โอดะ โนบูนางะ|tl|Oda Nobunaga|tr|Oda Nobunaga|uk|Ода Нобунаґа|ur|اودا نوبوناگا|vi|Oda Nobunaga|war|Oda Nobunaga|wuu|织田信长|xmf|ოდა ნობუნაგა|zh|織田信長|zh_classical|織田信長|zh_min_nan|Oda Nobunaga|zh_yue|織田信長|zu|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}}; in the Edo period, in the {{ill|Genna|de|Genna (Ära)|es|Genna|fa|گننا|fr|Ère Genna|id|Genna|it|Genna|ja|元和 (日本)|ko|겐나|ru|Гэнна|simple|Genna|sr|Гена|sv|Genna|tr|Genna|zh|元和 (日本)|qid=Q635245|lt=Genwa}} 4th year (1618), repairs were carried out by {{ill|Hachisuka Iemasa|ca|Hachisuka Iemasa|es|Hachisuka Iemasa|fa|هاچیسوکا ایه‌ماسا|fr|Hachisuka Iemasa|ja|蜂須賀家政|ko|하치스카 이에마사|zh|蜂須賀家政|qid=Q1073557|lt=Hachisuka Iemasa}}, and in the {{ill|Jōkyō|fa|جوکیو (دوره ادو)|fr|Ère Jōkyō|ja|貞享|ko|조쿄 (에도 시대)|ru|Дзёкё|simple|Jōkyō|sr|Џокјо|sv|Jōkyō|tr|Jōkyō|zh|貞享|qid=Q1146221|lt=Jōkyō era}} 3rd year (1686), when Atsuta Shrine was reconstructed by the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|ja|Tokugawa shogunate}}, similar repairs were made to this shrine{{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

The shrine building, originally in the {{ill|Owari-zukuri|ja|尾張造|qid=Q11465322}} style with a vermilion finish, was almost entirely destroyed by wartime damage in the {{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}} 20th year (1945) and was rebuilt in a form approximating its pre-war appearance in the {{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}} 38th year (1963){{Sfn|Takakurayui Mikoshi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1989}}.

=== Divine Rank ===
* Record of the conferral of divine Rank during the {{ill|Rikkokushi|cs|Rikkokuši|de|Rikkokushi|es|Rikkokushi|eu|Rikkokushi|fa|شش تاریخ ملی|fr|Rikkokushi|it|Rikkokushi|ja|六国史|ko|육국사|pt|Rikkokushi|ru|Риккокуси|simple|Rikkokushi|zh|六國史|qid=Q1151168|lt=National Histories}} period:
** On December 12, in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|de|Jōwa|es|Jōwa (período Heian)|fa|جووا (دوره هی‌آن)|fr|Ère Jōwa (Heian)|ia|Jowa|id|Jōwa|ja|承和 (日本)|ko|조와 (834년)|ru|Дзёва (Хэйан)|simple|Jōwa (Heian period)|sr|Џова (Хејан период)|tr|Jōwa (Heian)|uk|Дзьова (ненґо)|zh|承和 (日本)|zh_yue|承和|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} (836), it was listed among the renowned deities (as recorded in the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|cs|Šoku Nihonkóki|de|Shoku Nihon Kōki|es|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ff|Shoku Nihon Kōki|fr|Shoku nihon kōki|ja|続日本後紀|ko|속일본후기|pt|Shoku Nihon Kōki|zh|續日本後紀|qid=Q1041301|lt=Zoku Nihon Kōki}}) – noted as “Takakurayui Mikoshi.”
* After the era of the National Histories:
** Either Senior Second Rank<ref>[{{NDLDC|991014/413}} ''Shinja Kakoroku, Volume 1'' (Imperial Studies Institute, 1902, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 413 lines]</ref>, or Upper Senior Second Rank<ref>{{PDFlink|[https://websv.aichi-pref-library.jp/wahon/pdf/1103283156-001.pdf ''Domestic Shinmyōchō'']]} (Bunsei 13 [1830] transcribed combined edition, Aichi Prefectural Library “Precious Wa Books Digital Library”) 6 lines.</ref>, or Junior Second Rank{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}} (in the {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|ja|尾張国内神名帳|sv|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|zh|尾張國內神名帳|qid=Q11041830}}) – the inscription being “Takakura Myōjin” or “Takakura Myōjin”{{Sfn|Miya-ki|2012|p=28}}. Note that the Ranking varies among manuscripts.

== Subordinate Shrines ==
Within the precincts, the following four subsidiary shrines are enshrined<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>. In the early modern period, it is said that there were also the {{ill|Mitarai Shrine|ja|御手洗神社}} and the {{ill|Watatsumi Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|海神社|qid=Q123530063|lt=Kaijin Shrine}}.
* {{ill|Hokotori Shrine|ja|鉾取社}} – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Hokotori-no-Kami|ja|鉾取神}}

== Festivals ==
* Inari Shrine Festival (on Hatsu-uma day)
* Takakura Inari Kōsha, Spring Grand Festival (old Hatsu-uma day)
* Child Custody Festival (April 3)
*: A custom in which young children are entrusted to the enshrined deity until the age of 15, praying for healthy growth and protection from pests, with a subsequent thanksgiving visit once safely grown.
* Annual Festival (June 1)
* Mii Festival (on Doyō-iri day)
*: It is believed that if a child peers into the well of Mii Shrine on this day, it brings benefits of pest protection<ref name="HistoryDocument"/>.
* Takakura Inari Kōsha, Autumn Grand Festival (November 8)
